A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GNN+ study. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching appendix material relocated into the main text.

before.justification: v2 reports original GNN+ benchmark evaluations and component ablations in Tables 2-6, plus sensitivity experiments, additional comparisons and visual analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations and Appendix B experiments reported in v2.

M1.justification: GNN+ retains the same six enhancement techniques for GCN, GIN and GatedGCN. The architecture, update equations, readout and training objective in Sections 2-3 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 14 primary datasets and the five additional small graph-classification datasets in Appendix B.3: IMDB-B, IMDB-M, COLLAB, MUTAG and PTC. Tasks and test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including LDP, HRN, MTGCN and CO-GNN in Appendix B.3. The newly cited works in v3 are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A-B retain the same splits, metrics, parameter budgets, hyperparameter searches and testing procedures. The added wording about a shared hyperparameter search space in Section 6 describes prior work, not a changed experiment here.

E4.justification: Both retain the component ablations, depth and dropout sensitivity analyses, fixed-configuration tests, embedding visualizations and static-attention case study. Figure 6 is resized without changing the analysis.

E5.justification: Both report means and standard deviations from five independent runs with different random seeds. Uncertainty reporting in the tables and sensitivity plots is unchanged.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores, ablation results, runtimes and appendix findings are unchanged. For example, Table 3 reports GCN+ Peptides-func average precision of 0.7261 ± 0.0067 in both versions; Figures 3-6 retain identical image content.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations (1)-(12) are unchanged. Neither version provides theoretical guarantees or proofs; the revised discussion of missing theory does not introduce mathematical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the claims about enhanced classic GNNs matching or surpassing GTs, achieving top-three rankings across 14 datasets and first place in eight, with greater efficiency. The edited conclusion preserves the same contribution and claim scope.

C2.justification: v2 Appendix C.3 acknowledges the absence of theoretical explanation. v3 Section 7 retains this limitation and adds that existing benchmarks may inadequately represent real-world complexity and diversity, so the relative advantage of classic GNNs could change on more challenging application-driven benchmarks.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the PyG implementation, workstation with eight RTX 3090 GPUs, validation-based hyperparameter selection, detailed configuration tables and training times. Code access information and the MIT license are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Platonov et al. (2023) on evaluation under heterophily and Bechler-Speicher et al. (2025) on benchmark quality. It also clarifies the shared hyperparameter search space in its description of Luo et al. (2024b), while retaining the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: Appendix C.2 and C.3 become main-text Sections 6 and 7, with the conclusion renumbered to Section 8. The limitations and conclusion receive limited rewrites, and small corrections include FNN to FFN; the remaining narrative is essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 6 is reduced by approximately 5% in linear size, allowing Appendix C.1 to finish on page 21. Relocated discussion reflows the concluding pages and references; all six figures and 17 tables retain their content and numbering.

improvement.justification: The added benchmark-representativeness limitation more clearly bounds the empirical conclusions, and moving related work and limitations into the main text makes them easier to assess. These are limited improvements with unchanged scientific evidence; the slightly smaller Figure 6 is a modest presentation tradeoff.
